No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Pochettino Vows To Restore Man Utd As Manchester’s Kings by Affa Acho 6 minutes ago in Football , Sport Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to restore the Old Trafford club as Manchester’s most successful team, insisting that the city’s football rivalry will not remain dominated by neighbours Manchester City.
The Argentine made the bold declaration after taking charge of his final match as United States head coach, guiding the hosts to a 2-0 victory over Haiti in Cincinnati on Tuesday.
Pochettino, who is due to begin his new role on Wednesday after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract with United, was challenged by TNT Sports analyst DaMarcus Beasley following the match.
Beasley, who spent the 2006-07 season on loan at Manchester City, jokingly insisted that “Manchester is blue, it will always be blue”.
However, Pochettino was quick to dismiss the suggestion, responding: “No way, you will see. Give me time and that is going to change.”
The former Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur and Southampton manager is understood to have travelled directly to Manchester by private jet after completing his final assignment with the United States.
Speaking about his new challenge, Pochettino admitted that the task ahead was significant but expressed confidence in his ability to turn around United’s fortunes.
“We’re excited because the new challenge is big, but it’s the adrenaline that you want to feel,” he said.
“We are going to have a different job but we have the experience to deal with that. We need to add our common sense in the way that we are going to approach all the things.
“We know that it is not a situation that deserves to be at a club like Manchester United and for the fanbase.”
Pochettino leaves the United States national team after overseeing 37 matches, recording a 62.16 per cent win ratio.
During his spell, he guided the Americans to the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup final and the last 16 of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, which the country co-hosted.
Tuesday’s victory over Haiti also secured the United States a place in the CONCACAF Nations League semi-finals, providing a winning conclusion to his tenure.
In an emotional farewell message posted on Instagram, Pochettino expressed pride in his achievements with the national team, saying he hoped to have strengthened the players’ belief in their ability to compete against the best.
“I am proud of what we achieved. When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team,” he wrote.
“I am proud of what we achieved. When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team,” he wrote.
The 54-year-old described his time with the United States as personally and professionally rewarding but admitted that leaving was difficult.
“This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally. Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to.
“I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.
“I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves.”
Pochettino now faces the daunting task of rebuilding Manchester United and restoring the club’s status among English football’s elite, with his ambition to challenge Manchester City’s dominance already setting the tone for his Old Trafford reign.
